answer: The grove multiplier is published, charged in nebula, and trellis lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2409 identities would post 4439 proofs and burn roughly 30 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
